official.explanation: The correct answer is C. Figure 1a shows an ill-defined opacity in the right cardio-phrenic angle without any air bronchogram or signs of volume loss, ruling out pneumonia and collapse. Figure 1b confirms the presence of a depressed sternum (pectus excavatum), which can cause projection of anterior chest wall tissues over the lung, leading to the observed opacity. The absence of air bronchogram in Figure 1b further supports that this is not due to a true lung pathology.
